title: Implementation of Additional Export Controls: Certain Advanced Computing Items; Supercomputer and Semiconductor End Use (interim final rule, FR Doc 2023-22299)
publisher: U.S. Federal Register (Bureau of Industry and Security)
notes: October 2023 rule: removed the interconnect-bandwidth test, kept TPP 4,800 and added a performance-density test (TPP >= 1,600 with density >= 5.92 also controlled). Released 2023-10-17; publication date per govinfo package. Located via web search 2026-11-05; PDF not fetched (host not tested).

title: US Prohibits Exports of Nvidia's A800 and H800 to China, Blacklists Chinese GPU Developers
notes: October 2023 rule caught A800/H800 (built with NVLink cut to 400 GB/s to pass the 2022 600 GB/s test). Content via web-search result snippets.

title: ECCN 3A090/4A090: TPP and performance density explained
notes: Secondary explainer: 2022 rule = TPP >= 4,800 or aggregate bidirectional interconnect > 600 GB/s; 2023 rule = TPP 4,800 or TPP >= 1,600 with performance density >= 5.92, plus a lower notified tier. Content via web-search result snippets; check against the Federal Register text.

title: Nvidia's New China AI Chips Circumvent US Restrictions | H20 Faster Than H100 | Huawei Ascend 910B
author: Dylan Patel et al.
notes: Leaked H20 specs: ~296 TFLOPS FP8 / ~148 TFLOPS 16-bit (~15% of H100), 96 GB HBM3, ~4.0 TB/s, 900 GB/s NVLink; TPP ~2,400 (other reports ~2,500). Content via web-search result snippets; NVIDIA never published an H20 datasheet.

title: Trump says Nvidia will hand the U.S. 15% of its H20 chip sales to China
notes: 15% of H20 China revenue to the US government (Trump said he asked for 20%); AMD MI308 under the same arrangement; NVIDIA did not confirm the figure. Content via web-search result snippets.

title: Nvidia responds to claim China is urging local companies to avoid Nvidia H20
notes: Bloomberg-sourced: Chinese authorities sent notices discouraging H20 use, especially for government-related work. Content via web-search result snippets.

title: China's internet regulator tells Chinese tech companies to stop buying Nvidia AI chips - report
notes: FT report: CAC told ByteDance and Alibaba to stop testing and cancel orders for the RTX Pro 6000D (FT later removed 'all' Nvidia chips). Content via web-search result snippets.

title: China bans foreign AI chips from state-funded data centers
notes: Reuters-sourced (2025-11-05): new state-funded DC projects must use domestic AI chips; projects <30% complete must remove foreign chips or cancel orders; >$100B of state funding since 2021 (Reuters review of tenders). Content via web-search result snippets.

title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia China market share has fallen to zero
notes: Citadel Securities event 2025-10-06: '95% market share to 0%'; China previously 20-25% of DC revenue; Bernstein: NVIDIA China AI-chip share 66% (2024) falling to ~8%. Content via web-search result snippets.

title: China freeze on H200 chip sales clouds Nvidia's record earnings
notes: Q2 FY2027: H200 sales to Chinese buyers <1% of DC revenue; NVIDIA could not use its full US-licensed H200 quota because of Chinese objections; guidance excludes China DC compute. Content via web-search result snippets.

title: Nvidia incurs $400M charge from excess H200 inventory as single customer drives 16% of revenue
notes: ~$400M excess-H200-inventory provision (timing reported as Q2 FY2027 or over six months; Bloomberg-sourced). Lower-reliability outlet; confirm in the Q2 FY2027 10-Q. Content via web-search result snippets.

title: China clears first Nvidia H200 AI chips for import - sources (Reuters)
notes: Reported Beijing approval of first H200 imports during Huang's Jan 2026 visit; other reports said customs told agents H200s were not permitted. Content via web-search result snippets.

title: Nvidia reallocates China H200 manufacturing capacity for Vera Rubin chips - report

title: Nvidia's China Revenue: 19% Under Its New Count, Not 13%
notes: FY2026 10-K moved geographic revenue from billing location to customer headquarters (from Q3 FY2026) and recast FY2025 China from $17.1B (13.1%) to $25.0B (19.2%). Content via web-search result snippets.

title: Nvidia proves reduced dependence on China amid global shifts
notes: Secondary reading of the Q2 FY2027 10-Q: customers headquartered in China (incl. Hong Kong) $7.88B (~8% of revenue) vs $4.0B a year earlier; includes H200 and non-AI products such as gaming. Lower-reliability outlet; confirm in the 10-Q.
